At the heart of the internet is the internet protocol (IP) suite, which includes the TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) protocol stack. This stack includes several layers of protocols, including the network layer, the transport layer, and the application layer.

The network layer, also known as the Internet Layer, is responsible for routing data packets across networks. It uses a set of rules called the Internet Protocol (IP) to determine the best path for data to travel between devices.

The transport layer, also known as the Transport Layer, is responsible for ensuring that data is transmitted correctly and reliably between devices. It uses a set of protocols called TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) or UDP (User Datagram Protocol) to ensure that data is transmitted in a reliable manner.

The application layer is responsible for providing services to end users, such as email, web browsing, and file transfer. It is responsible for translating requests from end users into network requests and translating responses from the network back into end user responses.

In addition to the IP suite, the internet also uses other technologies, such as DNS (Domain Name System) to translate domain names into IP addresses and SSL/TLS to ensure the security of data transmitted over the internet.
